label: EXPLICABILITY_ARGUMENT_4: An argument rejects a proposed obtaining state because that obtaining…
definition: An argument rejects a proposed obtaining state because that obtaining would be inexplicable (PSR,p.2). Particular examples initially need only local rejection of inexplicability. The proposed extension to the existence of each thing has the unrestricted existence-explanation scope of his PSR; an analogy and demand for a principled boundary do not themselves specify a productive cause, concrete bearer or well-founded support relation.
note: Formal boundary: FIRST_PRINCIPLE_ENTITLEMENT_AND_PRESUPPOSITION_4 remains prose-only. Statements 91668b85-0bc9-5174-bc62-4fc812f80256 and 883da101-c728-57f7-a06e-8990fa384b6b distinguish local acceptance from dialectical warrant for extension. Neither has a Lean declaration or consuming argument at the audited baseline. An inference rejecting a particular state for lack of explanation is the intended pattern; demanding evidence for a belief is not by itself that inference. OPEN: specify which relevant similarities warrant extending rejection of inexplicability to existence, and what makes a restriction principled. The existing stanceMap and bridgeLadder supply conditional tests, not this warrant. See docs/notes/psr-self-application-756.md#five-sense-consumer-reconciliation-1659.
